note: Curated field map, not an exhaustive crawl of every GitHub toy named Cunning Claw. Stars drift; the architecture notes do not.

systems.name: OpenClaw
systems.take: Workspace files (SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md, USER.md), skills folders, heartbeat that stays quiet when idle, one messenger (Telegram), named brains with a cheap heartbeat model and fallbacks — not a sub-agent org chart. Since launch it has grown into the giant of the field: dozens of chat channels, native phone apps and a large community marketplace of add-ons. Reach is its strength.
systems.refuse: Curl-pipe installers, unauthenticated internet exposure, kitchen-sink plugin sprawl, defaulting every thought to Opus. Chasing its reach channel by channel: win on trust instead — watched on the glass, cards before consequences, honest about what was done.

systems.name: Hermes Agent
systems.take: agentskills.io SKILL.md, skills born from experience, MEMORY.md/USER.md, provider-agnostic brain, scheduled automations. Its real edge is skills that get better with use. Taken 29 Sept as skill lessons: one approved, dated line per lesson beside the skill, per machine, never rewriting the SKILL.md itself.
systems.refuse: Becoming a framework you assemble instead of an assistant you live with. No HUD, no machine-control soul. Rewriting instructions silently after every task: a skill is read back as orders, so each change passes an approval card.

systems.name: Open Interpreter
systems.take: Human-in-the-loop for shell. Excellent for one-shot local work.
systems.refuse: It is a power tool, not a persistent CUNNING CLAW. No heartbeat, no channels, no soul files.

systems.name: OpenClaw (Stanford)
systems.take: Local-first by default, cost/energy as first-class metrics, scheduled + continuous agents.
systems.refuse: Research platform weight. We are a production butler on one Linux machine, not PyTorch-for-agents.

systems.name: community daemon+sidecar projects
systems.take: Always-on daemon, authority gating, sidecar eyes on other machines.
systems.refuse: Nine-agent hierarchy and n8n-style workflow builders until the single operator loop is flawless.

systems.name: community HUD skins
systems.take: Proof the world wants an Iron Man HUD on a real agent, not a chatbot.
systems.refuse: Being a skin on someone else's runtime. We own the brain and the glass.

systems.name: LocalAI
systems.refuse: A model server is not an assistant.

systems.name: Classic Python CUNNING CLAW clones
systems.take: Wake word, TTS, the cultural brief: it should feel like CUNNING CLAW.

systems.name: Dragon Claw OS
systems.class: Forge lineage — agent in a box
systems.take: Local-first mini PC, voice, smart home, one-command install.
systems.refuse: Do not dissolve CUNNING CLAW into a distro. CUNNING CLAW is the mind; the OS is the house.

systems.name: Goose
systems.class: desktop agent + CLI (Agentic AI Foundation, Linux Foundation)
systems.take: Native desktop app on Linux, macOS and Windows plus a CLI; MCP as the extension standard; many providers including OpenRouter and Ollama. Proof that a serious open agent lives under neutral governance.
systems.refuse: A general-purpose worker you point at jobs, not an assistant that keeps the house: no heartbeat, no phone line, no soul files.

systems.name: Leon
systems.take: Tools, context and memory with a privacy-first stance, the same instinct as the loopback-only HUD.
systems.refuse: Years of rewrites: ship the loop that works on one machine and let it earn its features.

systems.name: AnythingLLM
systems.class: local agents + document chat desktop app
systems.take: Everything local unless you choose a cloud model: the default a cautious Linux user expects.
systems.refuse: A workspace for chatting with documents is not an assistant with hands on the machine.

systems.name: Self-Operating Computer
systems.take: One of the first full computer-use loops: look at the screen, move the mouse, type.
systems.refuse: Pixels first. Accessibility refs and real tools beat guessing coordinates, and a model driving the mouse needs cards before consequences.
